newsitem.title: GERMANY: Degussa eyes future with Veba -paper.
newsitem.headline: Degussa eyes future with Veba -paper.

text.p: Restructuring efforts at Germany's Degussa AG might be accelerated following a major shareholder reshuffle and could have an impact on the group's drugs business, chief executive Uwe-Ernst Bufe said.

Bufe told German daily business newspaper Boersen Zeitung that ongoing efforts to restructure the group's chemicals, health and nutrition businesses could be speeded up now that German utilities giant Veba AG, owns a 36.4 percent stake in Degussa.

Boersen Zeitung said Bufe indicated the new ownership structure might create new opportunities for Degussa's pharmaceuticals business Asta Medica, which posted sales of 1.4 billion marks ($811.4 million) in the 1995/1996 business year.
Degussa confirmed the comments Bufe made to the newspaper.

Noting that medium-sized drugs firms with annual sales of between five and eight billion marks still had room to thrive among the global industry giants, Bufe admitted Asta had some way to go before reaching that goal.

While Degussa officially stressed no decisions had been taken on what might be done with Asta Medica, saying all avenues were still open, industry sources have said Degussa has already made overtures to sell Asta Medica.
Asta Medica was not available for comment.

Bufe however told the Boersen Zeitung that Asta, posting a return on sales of around eight percent, does not number among the most profitable drugs groups. Thus it would make little sense to offer Asta for sale at the moment, the Boersen Zeitung reported Bufe as having said.

Only one year ago Degussa said it hoped to double its pharmaceutical turnover within two years moving it close to the annual turnover in its chemicals business. To help achieve this goal Degussa last year acquired U.S. drugs group Muro Pharmaceuticals.
Analysts say that Degussa might be well-advised to sell its drugs business as Asta's research pipeline is said to be rather thinly populated with new products.
At the same time Bufe said that Degussa and Veba were currently in the process of sorting out where the two groups might be able to cooperate in logistics or sales.
Bufe also said Degussa's shares, trading at 93 marks, were fairly priced at the moment.
